purpose: Prove a download-triggering action produces a REAL FILE on disk as an auditable evidence artifact — for a server-side file behind a download anchor, for a client-generated Blob behind a plain button that the DOM cannot distinguish from any other button, and for a hostile suggested filename that must not escape the artifact directory.
targeted_defect: BUG-M15-DOWNLOAD-NO-ARTIFACT — the browser context was created without a stated accept_downloads and no page.on('download') listener existed, so a click that downloaded a file produced no artifact, no filename, no content type and no record. The download simply evaporated: the crawl could not distinguish 'this button exports the policy schedule' from 'this button does nothing', which is exactly the P4 evidence the milestone requires.

expect_controls.why: a server-side file behind a download anchor — the href is captured, but only the browser event proves a file arrived
a CLIENT-GENERATED download: no href, so capture alone cannot tell this from any other button
its suggested filename is ../../../etc/audit-log.txt — application-controlled text that must never be used as a path component unreduced
an ordinary navigation — proves a link is not mistaken for a download

describes_runtime_behaviour.behaviour: clicking Download Sales Packet writes a non-empty file under the crawl's artifacts/ directory whose bytes begin %PDF-
clicking Export Policy Schedule captures the client-generated CSV even though nothing in the DOM declared a download
a hostile suggested filename lands INSIDE the artifact directory with its path separators reduced
each capture emits a browser_event with event=download carrying filename, bytes, content_type, page_url and the triggering control label

lane_note: The capture assertions adjudicate in both lanes (they are href/name/role facts). The behavioural expectations are playwright-only because jsdom has no download primitive and no filesystem sink; they are exercised by tests/browser/test_page_lifecycle_execution.py.
